title: Payment Arrangements — Counting the Days to the Schedule Anchor Date for a New Payment Method
content:
When a plan under Payment Arrangements moves to a new payment method, the days from the handling date to the plan's schedule anchor date — the count measured against the set-up notice — are counted according to the plan's most recent returned installment payment.

## Counting standard

- After a return for account closed or stop payment, the days to the schedule anchor date are counted in calendar days.
- After a return for NSF, they are counted in business days after the first business day following the handling date.
- After any other return, or with no return, they are counted in business days after the handling date.

A business day is a Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday. "In business days after the handling date" counts each business day after the handling date up to and including the schedule anchor date. "After the first business day following the handling date" counts the same way but does not count that first business day, and the count never goes below zero.

The return reason is read from the most recent returned installment payment on the plan's installment history; a plan with no returned installment payment is counted in business days after the handling date.

## The three counts side by side (hypothetical dates)

The handling date is a Monday and the schedule anchor date is the Monday fourteen calendar days later.

| Most recent returned installment payment | Count used | Days |
|---|---|---|
| Returned for account closed or stop payment | Calendar days | 14 |
| Returned for NSF | Business days after the first business day following the handling date | 9 |
| Returned for unauthorized debit or card chargeback, or no return | Business days after the handling date | 10 |

The business-day count of 10 is Tuesday to Friday of the first week (4), Monday to Friday of the second week (5) and the anchor Monday (1); the NSF count leaves out the first of those, the Tuesday.

## A short-range case

With the handling date on a Friday and the anchor date on the following Tuesday: the calendar count is 4; the business-day count is 2 (Monday, Tuesday); the NSF count is 1 (Tuesday only).
